rationale_c1: 487 consecutive patients diagnosed 2001-2009 at a single Dutch centre, with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, but only 216/487 (44%) had sufficient archived FFPE tissue for inclusion, and 3 further excluded for no invasive tumour in sample (final n=213) -- this tissue-availability filter is substantial and only partially explained.
rationale_c2: hrHPV by validated GP5+/6+ PCR enzyme-immunoassay for 14 types; HLA class I, PD-L1 (E1L3N clone, >=1% cutoff), CD8, FoxP3 and CD163 by IHC with named antibodies/clones/dilutions and standardized Ventana protocol (Table S1); CD8/FoxP3 quantified by semi-automated Image-J pixel counting with a fixed threshold.
rationale_c3: LNM and disease-specific survival status reported for essentially the full n=213 cohort (median follow-up 100.7 months); HLA class I assessed only on a 168-sample TMA subset due to insufficient tissue, a covariate-level limitation flagged separately by the authors, but the primary outcomes are close to complete.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic regression (LNM) and Cox regression (DSS) with backward stepwise selection and likelihood-ratio-test model comparison, adjusting for clinicopathological parameters (grade, pT stage, LVI) significant or near-significant in univariable models.
rationale_c5: IHC performed with a standardized Ventana autostainer protocol across the whole cohort, scored by two researchers plus an experienced uropathologist using a quality-control scoring system (Ruiter et al.); CD8/FoxP3 quantification used a fixed threshold applied uniformly via semi-automated image analysis.
criteria_note: Categorised as non_randomized (comparing hrHPV+ vs hrHPV- and other immune-marker groups with multivariable-adjusted inference), per MMAT_referencia_c1_c5.md guidance for comparative retrospective cohort studies.

rationale_c1: Consecutive series of all men with peSCC admitted to a single Chinese centre (SYSUCC) 1999-2013, with explicit eligibility criteria (histologically confirmed invasive peSCC, sufficient FFPE tissue, no other tumour occurrences, complete clinical/pathological data); n=178, single-centre and single-country.
rationale_c2: Nine immune markers assessed by IHC with named antibody clones/dilutions/catalog numbers (Table 5) and standardized digital image analysis (inForm); however, cutoff values for CD8, GrB, FOXP3, CD68, CD206, PD-1 and CTLA-4 were derived data-dependently via surv_cutpoint optimized against the disease-specific survival outcome itself, risking an optimistic/circular bias in the resulting prognostic associations.
rationale_c3: Follow-up complete for the primary DSS analysis (median 88 months, longest 209), but per-marker denominators vary because samples 'lost during processing or [with] no tumor epithelium' were excluded per marker without full quantification, and the clustering analysis excluded 15/178 (8.4%) patients for missing values without further detail.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression for DSS adjusted for T stage, N stage and hrHPV status alongside immune clusters (Table 2); multivariate logistic regression for LNM adjusted for tumour grade, T stage, LVI and histological subtype alongside immune clusters (Table 4).
rationale_c5: IHC performed with a standardized protocol per marker (Table 5), scored by two pathologists blinded to clinical data; quantitative image analysis applied uniformly via inForm software with consistent tumour/stroma segmentation across the cohort.
criteria_note: Categorised as non_randomized (comparing hrHPV+ vs hrHPV- and immune-cluster groups against LNM/DSS with multivariable-adjusted inference). The data-dependent cutoff selection for most quantitative markers (c2) is a notable study-specific limitation affecting most marker-level associations (though not the cluster analysis itself) -- worth flagging for Chaux at reconciliation.

rationale_c1: 108 patients selected solely on availability of adequate FFPE tissue blocks (1-4 blocks/specimen); no age, stage, treatment or geographic-origin data are reported for the cohort, so representativeness of the broader penile SCC population cannot be judged.
rationale_c2: IHC outcome measurements (PD-L1, FOXP3, CD8) are well described: named antibody clones/dilutions, standardized automated staining, antigen-retrieval protocols, and blinded dual-pathologist scoring with consensus resolution. However, the central exposure variable, HPV status, is not measured molecularly at all -- it is inferred purely from histologic subtype per WHO 2022 morphological criteria, a limitation the authors themselves flag and recommend resolving with direct HPV testing in future work.
rationale_c3: Marker-specific evaluable-spot denominators are highly unequal and largely unexplained: FOXP3 was quantifiable in only 80/528 spots (15%), versus 497-506/528 (94-96%) for PD-L1 and CD8, with no stated reason for the much greater FOXP3 attrition.
rationale_c4: No multivariable model or adjustment for confounding is presented anywhere: all associations (marker-marker correlations, and marker levels across grade/HPV-morphology/inflammatory-response strata) are bivariate (Spearman, Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn's with Bonferroni correction) with each clinicopathologic factor examined separately rather than jointly modelled; in addition, all tests treat individual TMA spots (up to 12 per patient) as independent observations with no adjustment for intra-patient clustering, which can further inflate the apparent significance of the reported associations.
rationale_c5: Staining and scoring were applied uniformly across the whole cohort via a standardized automated immunostainer protocol with fixed antibody dilutions and retrieval conditions, and expression was scored blinded to clinical data by two experienced pathologists with consensus resolution of discrepancies -- the exposure/marker assessment itself was administered as intended.
criteria_note: Categorised as non_randomized (single-cohort comparative study testing immune-marker levels across histological-grade, HPV-associated-morphology and host-inflammatory-response strata via Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn's tests, plus Spearman intercorrelations among the three IHC markers), consistent with this file's treatment of other single-cohort comparative IHC studies without a clinical-outcome endpoint (e.g. refs 17 Djajadiningrat, 18 Muller). Unlike most of this set, this paper has no survival/clinical-outcome endpoint at all -- the 'outcome' being appraised here is the immune-marker expression profile itself, and c4 additionally reflects the unaddressed spot-level clustering (multiple correlated spots per patient) noted in the extraction record.
assessment_note: This is the reference carrying the review's own conflict of interest (Alcides Chaux, R1, is a co-author of this primary study); appraised independently by R2 as required by the HANDOFF and the Reviewer 2 request. The primary study's own funding/COI declarations are clean (no external funding; no conflicts declared) and are unrelated to that meta-level review conflict.

rationale_c1: hrHPV- subset (60/158) was deliberately selected to profile against the parent hrHPV- cohort by pT stage and cause of death, rather than randomly or consecutively sampled; nearly all hrHPV+ cases (43/52) were included. This purposive matching, explicit in Methods, limits representativeness of the hrHPV- subgroup for unbiased comparison.
rationale_c2: hrHPV status by validated GP5+/6+ PCR enzyme immunoassay (14 subtypes); CD14, CD68, CD163 by IHC with named antibody clones/dilutions on an automated Ventana Benchmark Ultra stainer; myeloid densities quantified per spatial compartment using TissueStudio image analysis with a machine-learning tissue classifier.
rationale_c3: 13/103 (12.6%) patients excluded from the unsupervised clustering analysis for missing values, explicitly stated; primary compartment-density and survival analyses appear to use the full or near-full cohort with reasons given for exclusions.
rationale_c4: Competing-risk survival models were fitted with and without adjustment for hrHPV status, but the main compartment-specific hrHPV+/hrHPV- density comparisons (the paper's central finding) are bivariate (Mann-Whitney/Chi-square) with explicitly no correction for multiple testing ('deliberately, to avoid type II errors'), and grade/age/tumor-size associations with myeloid density are not mutually adjusted.
rationale_c5: IHC staining was automated and applied uniformly (Ventana Benchmark Ultra), but intratumoral/peritumoral regions of interest were manually selected by trained observers with no reported inter-observer concordance for this ROI-selection step.
criteria_note: Categorised as non_randomized (comparing hrHPV+ vs hrHPV- myeloid infiltration with some multivariable-adjusted survival inference). Shares its parent cohort (NKI 2001-2009 series) with ref 10 (Ottenhof 2018), already flagged in both extraction notes. Also noting for reconciliation: Alcides Chaux (R1 on this project) is listed as a peer reviewer of this article (not an author) -- not the COI relationship the HANDOFF defines for ref 12, but flagging for transparency.

rationale_c1: 57 retrospective PSCC cases (2010-2016) at a single US tertiary centre, all clinically node-positive or high-risk primary disease undergoing ILND; the text does not state whether this represents all eligible cases in the period or a further-selected subset, so consecutiveness cannot be confirmed.
rationale_c2: mIF with a 10-marker panel (CD20, CD3, CD4, CD8, CD45RO, CD68, CD206, CD163, NKp46, FOXP3) using a validated OPAL kit and standardized staining/scanning/analysis pipeline; HPV confirmed by p16 IHC plus Cobas HPV PCR; PD-L1 quantified centrally by Quickscore, though only at the TMA level, a limitation the authors themselves flag.
rationale_c3: Survival and density analyses use the full n=57 cohort with clear at-risk numbers reported in Kaplan-Meier curves; no substantial unexplained missing data identified.
rationale_c4: The main immune-marker survival findings (M1/M2 macrophage density and clustering, helper T-cell density and clustering) are reported as single-covariate Cox/log-rank analyses; no fully multivariable model adjusting these findings for established clinical confounders (nodal stage, HPV status, adjuvant therapy) is presented, only separate univariate clinical Cox modelling and stratified (not adjusted) subgroup analyses by HPV/nodal status.
rationale_c5: mIF staining, scanning and geospatial (Ripley's K, fixed-radius) analysis were applied via the same standardized, previously-published pipeline uniformly across all 57 samples.
criteria_note: Categorised as non_randomized (comparative cohort with survival inference by immune-marker density/clustering strata). Independent US (Moffitt) cohort, no shared-patient overlap with the Netherlands series (refs 10/13/26). Geospatial clustering radius given as '50 nanometres' in Methods, almost certainly a units error for micrometres -- already flagged in this reference's extraction note.

rationale_c1: 107 cases from a single centre (USTC); 60 archival (2011-2021) with no stated consecutive-collection criterion, plus 47 prospective (2021-2025); authors state tissue allocation to assays 'was dictated solely by real-time availability and technical feasibility, without any pre-selection based on clinical or biological features', which mitigates but does not confirm representativeness.
rationale_c2: HPV status by p16 IHC (ISUP-recommended criteria) plus SPF1/GP6++ PCR confirmation with explicit discordance rule (5 cases excluded); quantitative IHC scoring (0-4 scale, mean optical density) for CD138/IgA/IgG/PIGR/IFN-gamma; scRNA-seq via standard CellRanger/Seurat pipeline -- well-described, validated methods throughout.
rationale_c3: Main IHC cohort is 85/90 evaluable after excluding 5 HPV-discordant cases, but key sub-analyses show substantial attrition: IFN-gamma IHC performed in only 56/85 (66%) patients ('some samples had been partially or fully exhausted'), and bulk BCR-seq succeeded in only 16/20 (library construction failed in 4).
rationale_c4: All survival analyses presented (Fig. 2G, 3O-Q, 5H, 6O) are univariate Kaplan-Meier/log-rank comparisons; no multivariable Cox model adjusting for stage, age or grade is reported for any survival endpoint in the 85-patient cohort.
rationale_c5: Different subsets of the cohort underwent different assays -- scRNA-seq in only 23 tumours, IHC in 85, bulk BCR-seq in 20, flow cytometry in a further subset -- rather than a single protocol applied uniformly across the whole cohort.
criteria_note: Multi-modal translational study (scRNA-seq discovery + IHC validation + functional/mouse experiments) categorised non_randomized on the basis of the HPV+ vs HPV- comparative IHC/survival analysis, which is central to the paper's clinical claims. c5 reflects that different sub-cohorts received different assays by necessity (tissue-consuming single-cell work vs FFPE-based IHC), not a uniform single-method design.

rationale_c1: Retrospective two-centre cohort (Guangxi Medical University Cancer Hospital + Wuming Hospital) with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, but no statement of consecutive vs selective case ascertainment over the 2013-2023 collection window.
rationale_c2: TLS presence/absence was determined by H&E review alone, without IHC markers (CD3/CD20); the authors explicitly acknowledge this as a limitation: 'CD3+, CD20+, and other markers were not used to assess the presence or absence of TLSs, so there was a certain subjectivity.'
rationale_c3: Follow-up complete for all 83 patients (median 37 months, range 1-118, 14 deaths), with no missing data flagged for the primary cohort or outcome variables.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox regression including TLS, BMI, T stage, N stage and M stage as covariates (Table 3), with results also presented as a forest plot and nomogram.
rationale_c5: TLS density itself was quantified with a standardised method (tissue FAXS cytometry, fixed field/area formula), but the binary presence/absence call underlying the main analysis was a subjective read by two pathologists with a senior physician as tiebreaker, with no interobserver concordance statistic reported.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (TLS present vs absent, and TNM strata) with multivariable-adjusted nomogram (c4 solid). c2 is the dominant weakness here and is self-flagged by the authors in their own Limitations section as subjective TLS ascertainment.

rationale_c1: 185 archival cases (2000-2009, same surgical team) identified based on 'availability of sufficient material for TMA preparation'; 17 excluded for insufficient tissue (168 analysed) -- a tissue-availability selection filter, with no statement of consecutiveness in the original 185.
rationale_c2: Named, previously-validated antibody clones (HCA2/HC10 for HLA-A/B,C; anti-beta2m; MEM-E/02 for HLA-E; 4H84 for HLA-G) with a semiquantitative scoring system (Ruiter et al.) already validated by the same group in prior cervical-cancer work.
rationale_c3: 'Unknown' (failed TMA staining / no tumour in core) is substantial and spans every marker: beta2m 33/168 (20%), HLA-A 41/168 (24%), HLA-B/C 40/168 (24%), total HLA class I 45/168 (27%), HLA-E 38/168 (23%), HLA-G 28/168 (17%) -- not discussed as a specific limitation in the Discussion.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox model with HLA-A and total HLA class I expression measured separately against the strongest clinicopathological covariates (lymph node status, pT stage, grade, hrHPV) (Table 2).
rationale_c5: TMA-based IHC with 3 cores per case, uniform staining protocol across the cohort, semiquantitative scoring by a single experienced observer using a previously validated quality-control system (Ruiter et al.).
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (HLA expression strata vs survival, stratified by HPV status) with multivariable-adjusted inference (c4 solid). c3's 17-27% unaddressed missingness across all HLA markers is the dominant weakness.

rationale_c1: 60 archival cases from a single centre (Frankfurt); no statement of consecutive vs selective case ascertainment.
rationale_c2: Primary immune-cell-infiltrate score is a subjective 1-3 H&E read with no IHC markers, deliberately chosen 'to make our results reproducible to a wide range of pathologists regardless of their immunohistochemical repertoire'; the PD-L1 sub-analysis (n=30) used standardised IHC (clone ZR3, fixed protocol) scored by two pathologists blinded to clinical data.
rationale_c3: The primary immune-infiltrate score is complete for all 60 patients, but PD-L1 IHC was performed in only 30/60 (50%, 'with sufficient material') -- half the cohort missing for that key biomarker.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox regression with immune cell infiltrate, pT stage and their interaction term (Table 4), with proportionality assumptions explicitly checked.
rationale_c5: PD-L1 slides were scored by two pathologists blinded to clinical data with a fixed protocol; the primary immune-infiltrate score (1-3 scale) does not report blinding or interobserver concordance for its readers.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (immune infiltrate strata, PD-L1 subset) with multivariable-adjusted survival model (c4 solid). PD-L1 sub-cohort available in only half the patients (c3); primary infiltrate score deliberately non-IHC-based, a design choice the authors justify but that limits c2/c5.

rationale_c1: FMI database cohort of PSCC cases referred for routine-practice comprehensive genomic profiling, not a declared consecutive series or population-based sample; authors themselves flag 'potential bias toward European ancestry' in Limitations, indicating referral/selection bias relative to the broader PSCC population.
rationale_c2: Validated hybrid-capture CGP assay (FoundationOne/FoundationOne CDx) for genomic alterations and TMB; validated somatic-germline computational method; PD-L1 IHC with named antibody clone (22C3, Dako) and pre-defined TPS cutoffs; HPV detection by next-generation sequencing -- methods explicitly described and referenced.
rationale_c3: Primary TMB/genomic-alteration data complete for all 397 cases, but several covariates used in the TMB-based comparisons have substantial missingness per the Table's 'Missing' column: PD-L1 available in only 136/397 (34%), COSMIC signature in 87/397 (22%), gLOH in 256/397 (36%), with no discussion of how this incompleteness affects the low-vs-high-TMB comparisons that use them.
rationale_c4: Low-TMB vs TMB>=10 comparisons (genetic alterations, KEGG pathways, mutational signatures) are bivariate (Fisher exact/Wilcoxon with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction only), with no multivariable adjustment for age, genomic ancestry or disease extent, despite age approaching significance (P=.09) unadjusted.
rationale_c5: CGP performed using two different assay versions (FoundationOne: 395 coding genes vs FoundationOne CDx: 309 coding genes) pooled into the same analysis without explicit description of cross-platform harmonisation.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort design (TMB-low vs TMB>=10 mut/Mb as the primary contrast) categorised non_randomized despite the authors' own framing of the CGDB/OS component (n=30) as a 'descriptive study', because the genomic TMB comparisons drive the paper's main conclusions. Two pooled FMI assay versions not explicitly harmonised, flagged under c5. No interobserver concordance data reported for PD-L1 IHC reads.

rationale_c1: 134 patients (Jan 2009-Aug 2020) selected on the basis of paraffin tissue block availability ('for whom paraffin tissue blocks were available'), multi-institutional cohort with no stated consecutive-collection criterion.
rationale_c2: PD-L1 IHC with named clone (E1L3N, Cell Signaling), CPS scoring with a validated cutoff derived from the KEYNOTE-048 trial; pathologists blinded to clinicopathologic parameters when scoring PD-L1; p16/p53 IHC with named clones and positive/negative controls.
rationale_c3: Denominators are complete and internally consistent across all 134 rows for PD-L1/p53/p16 (table row sums close to 134 for each variable); median follow-up 44 months for OS.
rationale_c4: Explicit multivariate analysis for ORR/OS/CSS (HPV-associated subtype, p16, p16+p53 co-expression, nodal status) reported alongside univariate results.
rationale_c5: Same staining/scoring protocol (CPS, blinded reads) applied uniformly across all 134 samples.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (PD-L1-positive vs negative, low vs high CPS) categorised non_randomized. c1 (tissue-availability selection) is the only unresolved criterion.

rationale_c1: Single-centre retrospective cohort (University Hospital Kralovske Vinohrady, 2002-2022); all histopathologically verified invasive pSCC cases included 'regardless of history of neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy administration', but no explicit statement of consecutive ascertainment over the 20-year window.
rationale_c2: Two experienced pathologists blinded to follow-up; tumour budding scored per the International Tumour Budding Consensus Conference (ITBCC) 2016 criteria; lymphocytic infiltrate scored using a melanoma-adapted scheme; IHC with named clones (p16, p53, CD3, CD8, PD-L1, MMR panel) on a standardised Ventana BenchMark ULTRA autostainer; immunoscore quantified digitally (CaseViewer) per the Galon et al. method.
rationale_c3: Data are complete and internally consistent across all 152 cases for every reported variable (Table 1), with no relevant missingness flagged.
rationale_c4: Extensive multivariate Cox regression adjusting for age and associated covariates (Table 4), with multiple adjustment combinations reported for robustness.
rationale_c5: Same pipeline (autostainer, clones, quantification software) applied uniformly to all 152 cases.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (budding/infiltrate/p53 strata vs survival) categorised non_randomized. c1 (unstated consecutiveness over a 20-year single-centre window) is the only unresolved criterion.

rationale_c1: Four-centre cohort (2010-2023) with explicit inclusion criteria (bilateral rILND, definite pN stage, reliable preoperative blood work, clear outcome data), but no statement of consecutive ascertainment -- the completeness requirement itself introduces a selection filter.
rationale_c2: NLR/LMR/CRP/SAA measured preoperatively with ROC-derived cutoffs; IHC for TANs/CD4/CD8 with named antibodies; flow cytometry and multiplex IF with specific markers (CXCR2, CD66b, MPO, TIM3) -- solid, well-detailed methodology.
rationale_c3: SAA available in only 412/582 (71%, 'detection only conducted after 2017', explicit reason given); validation sub-cohorts are much smaller and heterogeneous relative to the main 582-patient cohort (167 for IHC, 42 for flow cytometry, 16 for mRNA-seq).
rationale_c4: Propensity score matching (1:1) to control confounders plus post-PSM multivariable Cox regression identifying NLR and pN stage as independent predictors -- a methodologically strong design.
rationale_c5: NLR is measured via routine preoperative laboratory testing, but no harmonisation of the analytic method across the four participating centres is specified.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (high vs low NLR) categorised non_randomized. PSM design (c4) is a real strength; c3/c5 reflect the disparity between the large primary cohort and much smaller mechanistic validation sub-cohorts.

rationale_c1: Authors explicitly state in Discussion: 'limited by its retrospective nature and potential selection bias as patients were mostly treated at academic centers and in countries where immune checkpoint inhibitors are available' -- an author-acknowledged representativeness limitation, not an inferred one.
rationale_c2: HPV status determined by 'either P16 immunohistochemistry or HPV DNA testing, depending on availability at each center' (Methods) -- non-standardised across the 24 participating centres; ORR assessed per RECIST 1.1 by the clinical investigator 'whenever feasible', with no stated central radiologic review.
rationale_c3: Primary endpoints (OS/PFS, n=92) reported with complete Kaplan-Meier at-risk tables and 85/92 (92%) response-evaluable, but key biomarker covariates central to this review's HPV focus have major missingness: HPV status known in only 49/92 (53%), PD-L1 in 26/92 (28%), TMB in 18/92 (20%), MSI in 32/92 (35%).
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox regression for both OS and PFS explicitly adjusting for ECOG performance status, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio, visceral metastases and number of prior therapy lines (Results, Multivariable analysis section).
rationale_c5: The exposure (ICI therapy) is deliberately heterogeneous across the cohort: pembrolizumab monotherapy, nivolumab monotherapy, cemiplimab monotherapy, and nivolumab+ipilimumab +/- multitargeted VEGFR-TKI combinations, spanning first-line through 4th-line settings, all pooled into the same primary survival analysis.
criteria_note: Comparative multicentre (24-site) cohort with multivariable-adjusted prognostic modelling (c4 solid). Missingness in HPV/PD-L1/TMB/MSI (c3) is particularly consequential for this review's HPV-stratification aim -- despite this, the study's own HPV+ vs HPV- OS/PFS comparison (n=17 vs n=32) found no significant difference, worth flagging for Chaux given the small stratified n. Authors' own acknowledgment of selection bias drives c1.

rationale_c1: Single-centre archival cohort (Mainz, 1996-2019) built from available FFPE tissue samples rather than a declared consecutive enrolment; authors themselves list 'varying duration of FFPE tissue storage' as a limitation, which is precisely a tissue-availability selection concern.
rationale_c2: Antibody clones, dilutions and platform well documented (CD3/CD4/CD8/CD20/CD56/CD138/FoxP3/PD-L1, all named clones; HALO digital image analysis with validated thresholding), but dichotomisation of every marker into low/high used the Charite Cutoff Finder optimised against the study's own survival data -- the same circularity concern already flagged for ref 11 (Chu 2020).
rationale_c3: Denominators vary by biomarker (Table 2: NA count 0-6 depending on marker/compartment) and by clinical covariate (N-stage missing in 11/93, 11.8%), with no discussion of how this variability affects the reported associations.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox regression for OS/RFS/DSS adjusting for tumour grading, stage and lymph node metastasis alongside PD-L1 CPS and the immune markers significant in univariate analysis (Table 4).
rationale_c5: Automated IHC staining (Dako autostainer) and digital quantification via the same HALO pipeline/thresholds applied uniformly across the whole cohort, as described in Methods.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (immune-cell density strata vs survival) categorised non_randomized. Cutoff-finder-based dichotomisation (c2) is a recurring methodological pattern across several refs in this set (10, 11, 26) -- worth flagging as a cross-study pattern for Chaux at reconciliation.

rationale_c1: Explicit eligibility criteria (confirmed PSCC pathology, AJCC8 advanced setting, definite HPV status, receipt of anti-PD1-based therapy), but single-centre/single-country cohort with no statement of consecutive vs selected enrolment.
rationale_c2: HPV assessed by qPCR, explicitly chosen over p16 IHC 'to avoid the possible missed diagnosis' (named kit, Hybribio), with a pre-defined PD-L1 TPS cutoff (5%) -- well-justified and standardised measurement approach.
rationale_c3: PD-L1/EGFR expression 'Unknown' in 24/87 (27.6%) of the cohort with no discussion of this gap's impact, though the primary efficacy/survival endpoints (ORR, PFS, OS) are largely complete with explicit reasons given for the 7 non-evaluable patients.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic regression for ORR and multivariable Cox regression for PFS/OS, adjusting for smoking, pathological grading and PD-L1 (Tables 4-5).
rationale_c5: 90.8% received the same triple regimen (anti-PD1 + chemotherapy + anti-EGFR), but four different anti-PD1 agents (toripalimab, camrelizumab, sintilimab, tislelizumab) are pooled without per-agent comparison, and first-line/multi-line settings are combined in some aggregate analyses.
criteria_note: Comparative cohort (HPV+ vs HPV- outcomes on PCT) categorised non_randomized; multivariable-adjusted (c4) is a strength. Missingness concentrated in PD-L1/EGFR (c3), not in the primary HPV/efficacy variables central to this review.

rationale_c1: Explicit eligibility criteria (advanced GU tumours lacking approved standard of care or refractory to prior therapy, measurable disease per RECIST v1.1) aligned with the research question of evaluating CaboNivo/CaboNivoIpi efficacy and safety.
rationale_c2: Small, heterogeneous histology subgroups pooled across dose-escalation (cabozantinib 40 vs 60 mg; nivo/ipi at 1 vs 3 mg/kg) and expansion cohorts; the penile-cancer subgroup (n=9-11) is particularly small to represent the target population.
rationale_c3: Response was investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1, with no stated independent central radiologic review.
rationale_c4: 12/120 (10%) patients not evaluable for response, with an explicit reason given for each (early progression, withdrawal, toxicity, refusal, restaging not yet reached) -- low, well-documented attrition, CONSORT-style.
rationale_c5: Appropriate statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, Cox, log-rank) for the exploratory single-arm design; authors explicitly acknowledge the small-sample-size limitation for between-treatment comparisons.
criteria_note: Phase I trial with non-randomized dose-escalation and expansion cohorts (CaboNivo vs CaboNivoIpi assigned by cohort, not randomized); categorised descriptive, consistent with the same-pattern classification used for refs 30/31/32 in this set (single-arm design, no randomized comparator). Penile-cancer-specific results (n=9-11) are hypothesis-generating only, as the authors themselves state.

rationale_c1: Prospective basket phase 2 trial with pre-specified eligibility criteria (histologically confirmed recurrent/metastatic SCC of specified primary sites, ICI-naive, ECOG 0-1, measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, adequate organ function) and per-cohort sample size determined using an A'Hern design based on cohort-specific hypotheses.
rationale_c2: Multicentre across France, Italy and Luxembourg, but the penile cohort (n=11) is explicitly flagged by the authors as small given disease rarity, with limited power and generalisability acknowledged as a study limitation ('Especially for the vulvar/vaginal and penile cancer cohorts, the number of patients included was small').
rationale_c3: RECIST 1.1 tumour assessment with centrally confirmed ORR as a secondary endpoint; PD-L1 by validated 22C3 IHC assay; HPV by real-time PCR with type-specific primers plus GP5+/GP6+ PCR and Sanger sequencing confirmation; WES via a standardized DRAGEN pipeline with matched tumour-normal samples.
rationale_c4: Trial-level CONSORT flow is well documented (112 enrolled -> 111 safety -> 107 efficacy, with reasons given), but biomarker completeness specifically within the 11-patient penile cohort is limited: TMB missing in 5/11 (45%) and PD-L1 CPS missing in 2/11 (18%), reported transparently in Table 1 but substantial for this subgroup.
rationale_c5: Per-cohort A'Hern sample-size design, two-sided exact binomial 95% CI for ORR, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards for PFS/OS, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons in genomic analyses; authors explicitly acknowledge limited power from small per-cohort n as a limitation, distinct from an inappropriate analysis choice.
criteria_note: Categorised as descriptive (single-arm basket trial reporting per-cohort ORR without a randomized comparator), consistent with the same-pattern classification used for refs 31 (HERCULES) and 32 (Xu 2026) in this set. All HPV/PD-L1/TMB outcome analyses (ORR, PFS, OS by biomarker status) are pooled across the six SCC primary sites in the trial, not penile-specific -- no penile-specific biomarker subgroup analysis is reported, consistent with the extraction_note already on file for this reference.

rationale_c1: Prospective phase 2 trial with explicit eligibility criteria (histologically confirmed advanced/recurrent/locally advanced PSCC, ECOG 0-1, measurable disease, adequate organ function) enrolling across 11 Brazilian sites; sampling matches the research question.
rationale_c2: Single-country (Brazil) academic-centre population; race distribution reported but trial eligibility criteria inherently select fitter patients than the full advanced-PSCC population; generalisability beyond Brazil untested.
rationale_c3: RECIST 1.1 with central review confirmation of ORR, CTCAE v5.0 for AEs, validated EORTC QLQ-C30 for HRQoL, NGS/IHC biomarker assays described in Methods.
rationale_c4: CONSORT diagram documents reasons for all screen failures and efficacy exclusions (3 active infection, 1 prior chemotherapy); discontinuations and causes fully itemised; only 2/37 (5.4%) lost to follow-up.
rationale_c5: Pre-specified sample size calculation (33 patients, 78.5% power, one-group exact binomial test) with Clopper-Pearson CI for ORR and Kaplan-Meier for PFS/OS matches a single-arm phase 2 design.
criteria_note: Single-arm phase 2 trial without randomized comparator classified as descriptive per MMAT_referencia_c1_c5.md (a single-arm phase II is not rct).

rationale_c1: Prospective two-cohort phase II trial with pre-specified eligibility (T4 or N2/N3 PSCC, ECOG 0-1, no distant metastasis, ICI-naive) at 2 centres; sampling targets the locally advanced resectable PSCC population the research question addresses.
rationale_c2: Small (n=25 of planned 28), two-centre, single-country sample; assignment to neoadjuvant-adjuvant vs adjuvant-only was by resectability criteria, not randomization, and the authors note the resulting selection bias reflecting real-world triage rather than a representative sample for between-group comparison.
rationale_c3: RECIST v1.1 confirmed by independent review committee or investigator; CTCAE v5.0 for AEs; PD-L1 CPS and p16 assessed centrally with pre-specified CPS>=20 cutoff.
rationale_c4: Attrition documented in the CONSORT diagram, but the source is internally inconsistent about the efficacy-analysis denominator: Abstract/3.1 state N=25, while Table 3 and the CONSORT diagram itself label efficacy outcomes 'N=24' -- this inconsistency limits confidence in the completeness of the efficacy dataset.
rationale_c5: Kaplan-Meier with log-rank test and Clopper-Pearson exact CI are appropriate for this exploratory phase II design; authors explicitly state multivariable analysis was not performed given limited sample size, an acknowledged power limitation rather than an inappropriate analysis choice.
criteria_note: Categorised as descriptive rather than non_randomized: although two non-randomly assigned treatment pathways are reported with exploratory subgroup log-rank comparisons, the primary analysis describes single-intervention efficacy/safety across the full cohort, and the authors explicitly frame the pathway-subgroup outcomes as exploratory/non-comparable given non-random assignment. Judgment call per the grey-zone guidance in MMAT_referencia_c1_c5.md -- worth a second look in reconciliation.
